title: Is your brain a filter? A model of changed consciousness

beats.narr: What if your brain works like a filter?
One model pictures the brain as a channel. Information comes from a deeper source, passes through the brain's filter, and becomes what you experience.
The filter has two dials. Bandwidth: how many brain frequency channels are open. And clarity: how clean the signal is, against the noise.
beats.title: Two dials

beats.narr: In a changed state, the authors assume bandwidth drops by nearly a third, and clarity is cut in half. These are assumptions, not measurements.
beats.title: Changed state, assumed

beats.narr: Run the numbers, and normal brain capacity comes out around three hundred and fifty bits per second.
beats.label: bits per second

beats.narr: In a changed state? Around one hundred and eighty. Roughly half.
beats.label: bits per second

beats.narr: Yet the strongest patterns, like slow waves across the whole brain, survive the drop. They match feelings people report in many changed states.
One big caveat. The starting numbers are assumptions. The paper doesn't prove the brain works this way. But it does make a testable prediction.
beats.title: Read it carefully
items: Not proof the brain works this way
But it makes a testable prediction
